info.title: Switch Frame Tap
info.author: Papux200
info.description: Stream your games to a PC at 1080p60
info.details:
Switch Frame Tap is a sysmodule that streams the game you are playing - picture and sound - to a Windows, Linux or macOS PC, with no capture card and no dock. It reads the game's finished frames and encodes them with the Switch's own H.264 encoder: native 1080p at 60 fps.

- Play a Switch Lite (or any Switch) on a big screen: a USB cable in handheld, or the network (Wi-Fi or the dock's LAN port) to play docked
- Game audio, also in games that block recording (optional), and recording to MP4 on the PC
- Native-resolution PNG screenshots on a button combo, also next to the system's Album screenshots
- Webcam mode: the Switch shows up as a USB camera, for OBS (H.264, 1080p60) or any camera app (uncompressed, 720p)
- Stream the HOME menu and the console's overlays too: the volume bar, quick settings, power menu and Tesla/Ultrahand menus (optional)
- Turn the Switch's screen off while you stream
- This manager app for the settings and to install the optional tools (Ultrahand, SaltyNX, ReverseNX-RT, sys-clk or Horizon OC), plus a Tesla/Ultrahand overlay; it updates itself from GitHub

Needs Atmosphere (firmware 21 to 23) and a viewer from the GitHub releases page: Windows, Linux, macOS or Android / Android TV. It reads the running game like a debugger; with cheats loaded for a game it reads through Atmosphere's cheat engine, which is slower.

changelog:
v0.7.15
v0.7.15: the Album and System Settings on firmware 23, no more latency spikes, and 60 fps in the Android app on TVs

- The Album and System Settings stream again on firmware 23.- Firmware 23 gives applets 33 MB less memory, so the stream paused the whole time the Album or System Settings was open. Now they stream (after a pause of about a second as they open) on a smaller memory loan, so a 1080p stream may drop to 720p until you close them. The keyboard inside System Settings still pauses the stream (no memory is left beside it), and the viewer now says "the keyboard is open". It comes back as soon as you close it.
- No latency spike every 3 seconds (33).- While streaming, the sysmodule wrote a line to the SD card every 3 seconds (and its stats every 20), and each write showed as a spike in the latency graph. It now writes nothing while a stream runs and saves the log afterwards. Thanks to vbezniskotempo for tracking it down.
- Android / Android TV: 60 fps on TVs (27, 32, and likely the flashing in 34).- When the app fell a few frames behind, it rebuilt its video decoder, which on a TV took long enough to fall behind again, so it showed about one frame per second. It now keeps the decoder and asks the console for a fresh keyframe right away. Thanks to johannbalili1026-cyber for the 30-then-60 fps clue.
- Linux viewer (by allyssonmoscoso, 30):- native Wayland on KDE Plasma, switch-frame-tap-viewer --check (prints the session, drivers, udev rule, USB devices and network), a log for the desktop launcher (/.local/state/switch-frame-tap/viewer.log), a hint when SysDVR still holds the console's USB, a software retry when the GPU decoder can't open a stream, and recordings in your Videos folder.

Updating:- open the Switch app's Updates- page (or unzip switch-frame-tap-0.7.15-switch.zip over the SD card root) and restart the console. Settings are kept. The PC viewers and the Android app offer the update when they open.


Switch Frame Tap is free and open source. If you would like to support it: buymeacoffee.com/papux200: https://buymeacoffee.com/papux200

0.7.14: stream the HOME menu and the console's overlays too (the volume bar, quick settings, power menu, Tesla/Ultrahand) - optional; a new look for this app; updates from the app (the PC and Android viewers update themselves too); the Android / Android TV viewer; opening the eShop from the HOME menu while streaming works again.
0.7.13.2: sound in games that block recording works on firmware 23.0 and 23.0.1 (the patch file for them was missing).
0.7.13.1: streaming no longer stops until a reboot after closing some homebrew apps (Sphaira, for example).
0.7.13: fixes a black screen after launching many apps in a row, and the boot crash on consoles with several sysmodules (it now starts about 30 s after boot, only if there is enough memory); uses about half the system memory; Super Mario Odyssey fills the stream; smoother over Wi-Fi.
0.7.12: new PC viewer design (one Settings panel), picture controls and a recording timer; turn the Switch's screen off while streaming; a few ms less latency at 1080p.
0.7.11: firmware 23.0 / Atmosphere 1.12; macOS viewer; pressing HOME while streaming no longer crashes manuals or the eShop; screenshots next to the system's, and a custom combo with the Capture button; GPU upscaling in the viewer.
0.7.10: game manuals, news and the eShop work with Switch Frame Tap installed (it holds no applet memory while not streaming).
0.7.9: streaming while cheats are loaded (through Atmosphere's cheat engine); Xenoblade Chronicles X and Fire Emblem: Three Houses fixes.
0.7.8: back to 720p at once when leaving docked mode, also in 30 fps games; firmware 21.x streams by default.
0.7.7: a webcam for any camera app; no more fatal on Atmosphere older than 1.11.2.
0.7.6: no zoom on fake-docked menu changes.
0.7.5: install the optional tools from the manager.
0.7.4: sound in games that block recording, built in.
